title: Observational study to evaluate recurrences and surgical or postoperative complications after surgical treatment of female stress urinary incontinence with DynaMesh®-SIS mesh implants
summary:
The present study is a non-interventional, retrospective, national, monocentric observational study with prospective follow-up in the course of regular surgical treatment of female stress urinary incontinence using polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) mesh implants (DynaMesh®-SIS variants) from the manufacturer FEG Textiltechnik Forschungs- und Entwicklungsgesellschaft mbH, Aachen.

The success of treatment, complications and their treatment are recorded for all patients in the form of standardised questionnaires. The expected average follow-up period is 8 years. This allows insights into the frequency of complications and recurrences (renewed incontinence complaints) in the long-term follow-up. Literature data with such a long follow-up period are very rare and yet essential in order to be able to assess the safety and effectiveness of the slings, which ideally remain in the body for a lifetime.
This systematic data collection enables an evaluation of the success of treatment over the long term.

interventions.name: Data will be collected from 200 female patients who underwent surgical treatment for stress incontinence using a DynaMesh®-SIS implant at the University Hospital Aachen between 2013 and 2018.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Women of legal age ≥18 years
• Patients who have undergone surgical treatment of female stress urinary incontinence using a DynaMesh® sling mesh implant
• Sufficient knowledge of the German language, both written and spoken.
• Patients who have consented to data processing
Exclusion criteria:
As this is an observation of routine clinical practice, no patients meeting the inclusion criteria will be excluded.
